title: Thermal Physics Adventure 3: Ideal gases and kinetic theory
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet pV = nRT and the kinetic model.
meta_desc: Physics — ideal gas law pV=nRT, kinetic theory, mean KE = 3/2 kT.
final_note: You learned pV = nRT links gas variables, kinetic theory derives p from molecular impacts, and mean translational KE = (3/2)kT.

concepts.def: p Pa, V m³, T K, R = 8.31

walkthroughs.body_html:
pV = nRT

p Pa, V m³, n mol, R = 8.31 J/K/mol, T K.

Or per molecule: pV = NkT, k = R/NA = 1.38×10⁻²³ J/K.

Assumptions: point particles, elastic collisions, no IMF, random motion.

For fixed n: p₁V₁/T₁ = p₂V₂/T₂.

Boyle: pV = const at fixed T.
Charles: V/T = const at fixed p.
Gay-Lussac: p/T = const at fixed V.

Always use Kelvin!

From mechanics + statistics:

p = (1/3)(N/V) m ⟨v²⟩

Mean translational KE per molecule: ½m⟨v²⟩ = (3/2) k T.

So at 300 K, mean KE ≈ 6.2 × 10⁻²¹ J. RMS speed of N₂: ~520 m/s.

International perspective: Maxwell + Boltzmann (UK + Austria) derived this 1860s-70s — early evidence for atoms.

options: Metres per second — it's the speed at which the universe expands.
km per second per megaparsec (km/s/Mpc) — recession speed per unit distance.
Light-years — it's a measure of cosmic distance.

mcqs.q: What does the cosmological redshift of distant galaxies indicate?
options: The galaxies are turning red because they are getting older.
Light-years — it's a measure of cosmic distance.
Space itself is expanding, stretching the wavelength of light from distant galaxies as it travels.
Galaxies are moving through space away from us, like objects flying outward from a centre.
